Chapter 8: Supporting Others Through Adversity
You know, grief and hardship are things we all face at some point. But how we show up for each other during those tough times? That can change everything.
There was a time when she felt completely alone in her own loss. That experience opened her eyes. She became much more sensitive to the struggles folks around her were going through. She wanted to be the kind of friend who truly showed up—the one who listened, who made room for both tears and hope.
Not long after, a colleague quietly shared about a recent divorce. The hurt was fresh, and the future felt so uncertain. She recognized that look—the mix of fear and exhaustion—because she’d seen it in her own mirror. But instead of jumping in with advice or trying to fix anything, she simply listened. She nodded, handed over a tissue, and gently said, “I’m here.” It was a small gesture, but sometimes, those are the ones that matter most.
Most people don’t realize just how powerful it is to witness someone’s pain without rushing in to change it. She learned that true support isn’t about having all the right words. It’s about being present. Sometimes, just sitting together in silence, sharing a meal, or sending a quick message—something as simple as, “I’m thinking of you”—can mean the world.
She also discovered the value of practical help. When a friend’s parent became ill, she offered to pick up groceries and run a few errands. These little acts of kindness eased the weight her friend was carrying, and sent a quiet reminder: you’re not alone in this.
Along the way, she realized there’s no one-size-fits-all approach to supporting someone. Everyone’s needs are a little different. What brings comfort to one person might not help another. So, she started to ask, “What would be most helpful right now?”—and then, she respected the answer, even if it was just giving someone a bit of space.
Over time, she found that reaching out to help others was also helping her heal. Whether it was her time, her attention, or just a little compassion, the act of giving created a sense of connection and purpose. It reminded her—and maybe all of us—that even in the middle of pain, there’s always something we can offer.
